outcome: Microbiological characteristics of severe ophthalmia neonatorum (ON)
cohort: 1397 neonates with ON treated at Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University from January 2015 to December 2019
finding: Staphylococcus was the most common pathogen of severe ON, and nasolacrimal duct obstruction, meconium aspiration syndrome, and cesarean section were identified as risk factors for severe ON, while neonatal ocular prophylaxis was found to be protective.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a risk factor for severe ON.
